title: Knowledge Distillation with Perturbed Loss: From a Vanilla Teacher to a Proxy Teacher

problem.claim: Knowledge distillation typically trains a student to imitate a teacher's output distribution through KL divergence.

gap.claim: The KL-based objective can be sub-optimal because the teacher's output distribution may differ from the ground-truth label distribution, making blind imitation unreliable.

contributions.claim: The work proposes PTLoss, a knowledge-distillation objective formed by representing the vanilla KL-based loss with a Maclaurin series and perturbing its leading-order terms.
PTLoss implicitly transforms the vanilla teacher into a proxy teacher whose distribution is closer to the ground-truth distribution.
The work establishes a theoretical connection between distribution closeness and student-model generalizability, supporting principled selection of PTLoss perturbation coefficients.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly characterize PTLoss as a novel knowledge-distillation objective.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on six public benchmark datasets report that PTLoss is effective with teachers of different scales.

narrative_sequence.summary: Knowledge distillation transfers knowledge from a large teacher model to a small student model, commonly through KL-divergence matching.
Teacher outputs may differ from ground-truth labels, so blindly matching them can hurt student performance.
PTLoss perturbs leading terms of a Maclaurin representation of the vanilla KL-based loss.
The perturbed objective creates a proxy-teacher interpretation and connects distribution closeness to student generalizability.
The authors report effectiveness across six public benchmark datasets and teacher scales.

source_observation.claim: Teacher predictions can be unreliable when their distribution differs from the ground-truth label distribution.

interpretation.claim: A student may benefit from selectively correcting or reshaping teacher supervision instead of reproducing it exactly.

application.claim: When designing distillation objectives, evaluate whether the teacher signal is aligned with target-label structure before enforcing direct imitation.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish when the proxy-teacher transformation fails or how its benefits vary across tasks.

unknowns: The six benchmark datasets, model architectures, and teacher-student configurations are unspecified.
No quantitative results, baselines, metrics, or statistical details are provided.
The perturbation coefficients and their selected values are unspecified.
The abstract does not describe limitations, failure cases, or computational cost.
